qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Catarina Martins (The Left) Subject:

On 23 September 2026, nine Sahrawi political prisoners (including Naâma Asfari), who had been arbitrarily detained following the Gdeim Izik protests and dispersed across various prisons, began a hunger strike in response to Morocco’s failure to honour previous commitments. The detention of these human rights defenders has been condemned by bodies such as the UN Committee against Torture (2016) and the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention12. In view of the EU’s commitments under international law and bilateral agreements: 1.

What immediate diplomatic measures is the Vice-President/High Representative taking to ensure that the strikers receive urgent medical assistance, that fundamental rights are respected, and that the commitments made are honoured?
How is the EU Delegation in Rabat monitoring the situation, and will it demand the immediate release of those detained, in line with UN decisions?

How does the VP/HR reconcile diplomatic and trade relations with Morocco and the ongoing violations of international humanitarian law in Western Sahara and noncompliance with UN human rights mechanisms?
